title: Kyle — The Salt Flats
source: original film in the desert-racing tradition; visual references supplied by Kevin
notes: Sixth LoRA-driven film. First one whose subject is motion itself, which inverts lindsey_sparky's problem: engines, dust, heat haze and crowd give every long take its own movement. Faces live in s2 and s6 only. The genre's usual engines-on-tow-cables silhouette is deliberately replaced by a rigid outrigger chassis — a trailing cable is the single most reliable failure in this repo. The racer master is a reference image Kevin supplied (raw/racer_reference.jpg) rather than a generated one: three generated attempts put the exhaust flame on the forward intakes, and a control image settles the design far more cheaply than more prompt wording. The pilot had to be written in explicitly for s1/s4/s5/s7: a generic 'pilot' rendered as an adult every time, per still-geometry §2, and only a stated age plus the cockpit as a scale referent produced a child. That costs some machine fidelity against the supplied master — the long pilot paragraph pulls attention off the chassis — and the trade was taken deliberately. STOPPED 2026-10-04 at Kevin's request, four clips into the eight-clip run (s1-s4 rendered, s5 interrupted). All eight stills are picked and locked; the spec is complete and `check` passes, so the film can be resumed with `film_run.py kyle_saltflats clips`.

locks.subject: kyle_kx boy, a nine-year-old boy with child proportions, this exact face, short dark hair
locks.wardrobe: a cracked tan leather flight cap fastened close at the jaw with round brass-rimmed goggles pushed up on his forehead, a sand-coloured canvas racing tunic with a high collar sitting close at his neck, and worn leather gloves
locks.racer: A home-built desert racer: two enormous weathered steel turbine engines mounted on short rigid outriggers on either side of a slender central hull, positioned well forward so the engine intakes lead and extend past the front of the cockpit. The forward intakes are wide dark open throats with a smooth cone hub at the centre and turbine blades behind it, drawing air in, carrying no flame at all. Ribbed corrugated engine casings, exposed cooling fins, riveted patch plates and burnt bare metal, short hoses strapped tight along the housings. A small open cockpit with a bare seat and a low windscreen sits between and behind the engines on the central spar, everything bolted solid with no tow cables and no trailing lines. The only fire is a hot red exhaust plume blasting straight backwards out of the rear nozzles behind the machine. The whole machine hovers a clear metre above the ground with an unbroken band of open air beneath it from end to end, a blue-white repulsor glow washing down onto the ground under the hull, and its hard shadow falling on the ground directly below. It has no wheels, no tyres, no axles and no landing legs — nothing touches the ground anywhere
locks.flats: a vast blinding white salt flat under a huge pale dawn sky, low red sandstone mesas strung along the horizon, heat shimmer rising off the crust in the far distance
locks.arena: a start line cut into a sandstone canyon, tiered stone terraces packed with a distant crowd, tall weathered banners on poles, engine haze drifting across the open ground

locks.pilot: In the open cockpit sits kyle_kx boy, a small nine-year-old boy with child proportions, this exact face, wearing a cracked tan leather flight cap fastened close at the jaw with round brass-rimmed goggles down over his eyes and a sand-coloured canvas racing tunic. He is unmistakably a small child in a machine built for someone far bigger: his head and shoulders barely clear the low wind fairing, the seat back rises well above his head, his arms are short against the controls, and his small frame leaves the cockpit looking half empty around him.
